subject: Sprintwise capacity prioritization: Mar 27 handoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rachael Cole <rachael@octaveanalytics.com>
Cc: sales_ops@octaveanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sprintwise capacity prioritization: Mar 27 handoff

Team / Rachael —

Kicking off this week’s capacity handoff. Our ask: align on which deals in the pipeline we should prioritize for Dedicated capacity across the next two sprints (weeks). Attached is a trimmed pipeline snapshot (columns: deal, forecast pct, requested GPU slots, requested start). I’d like us to come out of this thread with a prioritized list and a concrete slot allocation we can commit to for the upcoming sprint.

Quick context/highlights from sales:
- Octave Analytics (Rachael) is requesting 16x A10 slots starting Apr 10 for a 12-week pilot (pooled inference for real-time dashboards). They are at procurement stage and expect a PO by Apr 3 if pricing holds.
- Two smaller deals (mid-MMR) are flexible on start dates but want guaranteed burst capacity in May.

Questions for infra & finance:
1) Marcus — what’s our available committed slot runway for Apr 10 start? Include reserved vs burst breakdown.
2) Laura — assuming Octave moves to PO on Apr 3, what’s the earliest we can approve a pricing/commit that preserves margin?
3) Karthik/Soojin — any latency SLO concerns if we place Octave in the same pool as other analytics customers?

Attachments: pipeline_snapshot_20280327.csv (trimmed export).

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus to propose an allocation by EOD today.
- Laura to flag any finance approvals needed for a mid-quarter reserved commitment.
- Rachael to confirm PO timing so we can pin a start date.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rachael Cole <rachael@octaveanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise capacity prioritization: Mar 27 handoff

Ben —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary from infra capacity planning after a first pass of the snapshot:
- Apr 1–14 reserved pool (US-west) has ~24 A10-equivalent slots uncommitted (after current reserved allocations).
- Burst capacity (on-demand) can cover short spikes up to ~40 slots, but sustained burst beyond 10–12 slots risks higher spot pricing and potential throttling during region-wide demand.

For Octave’s request (16x starting Apr 10):
- We can cover 12 slots from reserved uncommitted capacity and 4 via burst if we keep the pilot to 8–10 TPS steady-state.
- If Octave needs a hard-commit of 16 reserved slots, we need a signed commitment by EOD Apr 2 to convert a burst slot into reserved (lead time to reassign capacity: ~7 days).

Requested info from sales/finance to finalize:
- Laura: if we approve converting 4 burst -> reserved for a 12-week term, what’s the minimum margin threshold we need to hit?
- Ben/Rachael: can Octave accept a hybrid commitment model (12 reserved + 4 burst cap) for the pilot? That reduces our reserved exposure while meeting start date.

Notes: placing Octave in the same pool as other analytics tenants is ok from a network/placement perspective; we’ll isolate KV caches per customer. I’ll schedule a 20-min infra huddle at 2pm to validate reclamation windows if we need to reassign reserved capacity.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rachael Cole <rachael@octaveanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise capacity prioritization: Mar 27 handoff

Team —

From finance viewpoint: converting 4 burst -> reserved for a 12-week pilot is workable but we need the commercial terms to meet our minimum ARPU threshold for Dedicated offerings. I’ve attached the latest PRICING vignette that shows the reserved discount schedule and the minimum committed term we can offer without additional approval.

If Octave signs the PO by Apr 3 and accepts the hybrid model (12 reserved + 4 burst), we can authorize the reservation under standard terms. If they require full 16 reserved from day one, we’ll need a margin uplift (we typically require ~12% incremental margin to justify converting short notice burst into reserved capacity mid-quarter) and that will need VP finance sign-off.

Action items:
- Ben/Rachael: confirm model preference (hybrid vs full reserved) by EOD Apr 2.
- Marcus: if we go hybrid, outline which reserved slots are earmarked so we can set the pool tagging before Apr 10.

Attachment: reserved_capacity_pricing_v2.pdf

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Rachael Cole <rachael@octaveanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise capacity prioritization: Mar 27 handoff

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our timeline. A few notes from Octave:
- We expect procurement to return a PO by Apr 3 (working with internal legal). Happy to take the hybrid model for the pilot if that’s the most pragmatic path.
- Can Redwood provide a short-term SLA addendum for the pilot window to reassure our ops team? If so, we can sign the PO faster.
- Also want to lock in a short runbook on expected cold-start latencies and KV cache warming expectations. If you can share that (even bullets), we’ll include it in our ops checklist.

Proposed: Ben, can we schedule a 15-minute handoff tomorrow (Mar 28) to confirm exact start date and finalize pricing language? 10:00am or 3:00pm PT both work for me.

Rachael Cole
Head of Data Platforms, Octave Analytics
rachael@octaveanalytics.com | +1 206-555-0199
